checks.do: Whether the tenant skipped all or part of guided onboarding, since the skipped parts must be configured manually.
Before reporting automatic crash reporting as on or off, name that the onboarding page and the Client Connector page differ.

for-new-tenants.statement: The onboarding workflow is for new tenants: it is a streamlined workflow to add users, distribute the Zscaler Client Connector app and secure traffic by enabling policies that Zscaler recommends as a best practice.

quotes: Streamlined onboarding workflow for new tenants to add users, distribute the Zscaler Client Connector app, and secure traffic by enabling policies that are recommended by Zscaler as a best practice.

steps-and-skip.statement: Guided onboarding has four steps (set up users, set up traffic forwarding, set up security policies, fine-tune the security setup); Skip bypasses all or part of it and goes directly to the Experience Center home page, and the skipped parts must then be configured manually.

quotes: Step 1: Set up users.
Step 2: Set up traffic forwarding.
Step 3: Set up security policies.
Step 4: Fine-tune your security setup.
You can click Skip to bypass all or part of the guided onboarding setup and go directly to the Experience Center home page. You must then manually configure the skipped parts of the setup.

test-security.statement: The Test Security button checks the status of the current security configuration, to show current vulnerabilities, using Zscaler's Internet Threat Exposure Analysis, and the test can be returned to after onboarding to see how the organization is protected.

quotes: Click the Test Security button to check the status of your current security configuration to understand your current vulnerabilities using Zscaler's Internet Threat Exposure Analysis.
You can return to this test after you complete the onboarding process to see how you are protected.

onboarding-roles.statement: During onboarding a user is either an End User, a regular user who does not require administrator access, assigned to the Authentication Service Dynamic Group Registered Domains group, or a Full Admin, an administrator with full access to add, edit, import and delete users within the Zscaler Admin Console, assigned to the Authentication Service Global Administrators group and commonly called a super admin.

quotes: End User: A regular user who does not require any administrator access. These users are assigned to the Authentication Service Dynamic Group Registered Domains group.

Full Admin: An administrator with full access to add, edit, import, and delete users within the Zscaler Admin Console. These users are assigned to the Authentication Service Global Administrators group.
This type of user is commonly called a super admin.

add-user-methods.statement: While onboarding to Experience Center for the first time, a super admin can import users via the identity provider (IdP), import user details using a CSV file, or add individual users.

quotes: While onboarding to Experience Center for the first time, as a super admin, you can import users via your identity provider (IdP), import user details using a CSV file, or add individual users.

idp-import.statement: The page says to ensure the IdP is set up for SAML authentication and SCIM provisioning. The connection takes a unique name, a Domain (selected from the domains associated with the Authentication Service account), a Login ID Attribute (the IdP attribute used as the Authentication Service login ID) and a protocol, OIDC (Redirect URI filled in automatically, Client ID, Client Secret, Metadata URL) or SAML (SP Entity ID and SP URL filled in automatically, Metadata URL); for SAML, Fetch next to the Metadata URL box retrieves the metadata and the IdP Entity URL, IdP Single Sign-On URL and IdP Certificate are then displayed.

quotes: You need to ensure your IdP is set up for SAML authentication and SCIM provisioning.
A unique name for this IdP connection
Domain: Select the domain associated with the tenant for this connection from the drop-down menu. This list is generated from the domains associated with your Authentication Service account.
Login ID Attribute: Enter the attribute from your IdP that will be used as the Authentication Service login ID.
Select the protocol for your IdP, either OIDC or SAML then complete the information to retrieve the metadata:
Redirect URI: Filled in automatically.
Client ID: Enter ID to log in to the IdP.
Metadata URL: Enter the URL to retrieve metadata on your IdP.
Client Secret: Enter the secret associated with the client ID.
SP Entity ID: Filled in automatically.
SP URL: Filled in automatically.
Metadata URL: Enter the URL to retrieve metadata from your IdP.
Click Fetch next to the Metadata URL box.
Zscaler retrieves the metadata information required to connect your users.
IdP Entity URL: The unique URL for this IdP entity.
IdP Single Sign-On URL: The SSO URL to which users are sent for authentication for this IdP.
IdP Certificate: The certificate used to verify the digital signature of the IdP.
SAML Connection
The following IdP information is displayed:

idp-provisioning.statement: Under Provisioning, Generate Token generates a bearer token used by the IdP to connect to Zscaler, or a toggle skips the step and disables SCIM provisioning; the Disconnect <IdP Name> link at the top of the page removes all imported users from Zscaler and cannot be undone.

quotes: Under Provisioning, click Generate Token to generate a bearer token, which is used by the IdP to connect to Zscaler.
Click the toggle if you want to skip this step and disable SCIM provisioning.
If you want to remove all imported users from Zscaler, click the Disconnect <IdP Name> link at the top of the page. This action cannot be undone.

csv-upload.statement: The onboarding CSV template's header row is Action, Login Name, Display Name, First Name, Last Name, Primary Email, Secondary Email, Language, Department, Timezone, Password Reset and Group Names. A + row adds a user and needs values in at least Primary Email, Login Name, First Name and Last Name; a - row deletes a user and needs only the Login Name. The first line is retained as the header row, the file name has a .csv extension, each user is on a separate line with an email address whose domain name was defined in the Zscaler Admin Console, the password can be left blank to avoid uploading passwords in clear text, and one-time passwords can let users log in and set passwords.

quotes: Action,Login Name,Display Name,First Name,Last Name,Primary Email,Secondary Email,Language,Department,Timezone,Password Reset,Group Names
+ (plus sign) To add a user, enter values in at least the Primary Email, Login Name, First Name. and Last Name columns.
- (minus sign) to delete a user, you need only enter the Login Name of the user you are deleting.
Retain the first line of the file as the header row.
The file name must have a .csv extension.
Each user must be on a separate line.
Each user's email address must have a domain name that was defined in the Zscaler Admin Console.
The password can be left blank if you don’t want to upload passwords in clear text.
You can use one-time passwords to enable users to log in and set passwords.

csv-example-groups.statement: The template's example row puts the group names Group1, Group2 and Group3 after the Password Reset value.

quotes: Action,Login Name,Display Name,First Name,Last Name,Primary Email,Secondary Email,Language,Department,Timezone,Password Reset,Group Names
+,psmith@example.com,Priya Smith,Priya,Smith,psmith@example.com,,English (US),Engineering,(UTC+00:00) GMT,true,Group1,Group2,Group3

csv-email-rules.statement: If the authentication method is a one-time token or one-time link, the Primary Email field must contain a valid email address; the Secondary Email can specify any domain, but it must be a valid email address.

quotes: If the authentication method is a one-time token or one-time link, then the Primary Email field must contain a valid email address.
The Secondary Email can specify any domain, but it must be a valid email address.

individual-users.statement: Adding a user individually takes the user's first and last name and email address within the organization, and the role to assign; end-user entitlements are viewed at Administration > Entitlements > End User Entitlements and admin entitlements at Administration > Admin Management > Role-Based Access Control > Administrative Entitlements.

quotes: Enter the user's first and last name and their email address within your organization.
Select the role you want to assign to this user:
Go to Administration > Entitlements > End User Entitlements to view the entitlements.
Go to Administration > Admin Management > Role-Based Access Control > Administrative Entitlements to view the admin entitlements.

editing-users.statement: After users are onboarded and before onboarding is completed, their details can be edited (name, email address, or role between End User and Full Admin) or the users deleted; at least one user must be a Full Admin, and deleting or removing admin privileges from the only Full Admin prompts the admin to select a different user to become a Full Admin; individual users imported from an IdP cannot be deleted.

quotes: After you have onboarded users to Experience Center, you can edit the user details or delete users before completing the onboarding process.
click the Edit icon next to a user to change the user's name, email address or change the user role between End User or Full Admin

At least one user in your organization must be a Full Admin. If you delete or remove admin privileges from the only Full Admin user, you are prompted to select a different user to become a Full Admin.
You cannot delete individual users that were imported from an IdP.

roles-after-onboarding.statement: During onboarding users can only be assigned the Full Admin or End User role; after onboarding is completed any Full Admin can assign users to other admin roles in the Zscaler Admin Console, and user details are updated on the Users page (Administration > Identity > Authentication Service > Users).

quotes: During onboarding, you can only assign users to either the Full Admin or End User role. However, after you complete onboarding, any Full Admin can assign users to other admin roles in the Zscaler Admin Console.
After completing the onboarding process, you can update user details by going to the Users page (Administration > Identity > Authentication Service > Users) in the Zscaler Admin Console.

traffic-forwarding.statement: In the traffic forwarding step the admin sends users a link to install Zscaler Client Connector, and users must have administrator permissions on their devices that allow them to install applications; the platforms are selected on the Clients page; if a VPN is in use, its IP addresses and hostnames are entered so that Zscaler ignores traffic to those addresses and the VPN continues to work; and by default users receive automatic software updates to Client Connector, which a toggle disables.

quotes: Users must have administrator permissions on their devices that allow them to install applications.
you'll send those users a link to install Zscaler Client Connector
On the Clients page, select the checkboxes for the applicable platforms for your users.
If you're using a VPN, select Yes and enter the IP addresses and hostnames for the VPN. Zscaler will ignore traffic to those addresses so that the VPN can continue to work.
select the users who you want to receive an email containing a link to download Zscaler Client Connector
By default, users receive automatic software updates to Zscaler Client Connector. Disable the toggle if you do not want users to receive automatic updates.

policy-types.statement: The onboarding security policies are URL Filtering (block, isolate or allow internet destinations by URL category), SSL/TLS Inspection (configure what types of SSL/TLS traffic is inspected), Cyber Threat Protection (review additional protection policies for cyber threats such as botnets, phishing and malware), Data Protection (review policies that ensure sensitive data is not inadvertently leaked) and Privacy (configure how users' personally identifiable information (PII) is protected), with Miscellaneous settings to block countries and to add the company logo to banners, emails and user notifications.

quotes: URL Filtering: Block, isolate, or allow internet destinations by URL category.
SSL/TLS Inspection: Configure what types of SSL/TLS traffic is inspected for added security.
Cyber Threat Protection: Review additional protection policies for cyber threats, such as botnets, phishing, and malware.
Data Protection: Review data protection policies that ensure sensitive data is not inadvertently leaked via email, social media, file sharing, or other means.
Privacy: Configure how you protect your users' personally identifiable information (PII).
Block countries: Block internet traffic from specific countries
Add your company logo to banners, emails, and notifications: Add your company logo to banners, emails, and user notifications sent from Zscaler

url-filtering.statement: The onboarding URL Filtering page shows a recommended setup, and predefined URL categories are dragged to the Block, Isolate or Allow columns: blocked categories cannot be accessed, isolated categories open in a remote browser in a Zscaler data center so no active content from the web page reaches the user's device, and allowed categories open normally within the user's browser.

quotes: After you have set up users and traffic forwarding, click Set Up Policies.
URL Filtering policies allow you to use predefined URL categories to determine how internet traffic in each of the categories is handled by Zscaler.
Block: Websites belonging to blocked categories cannot be accessed by users in your organization.
Isolate: Websites belonging to isolated categories open in a remote browser in a Zscaler data center, preventing any active content from the web page from reaching the user's device.
Allow: Websites belonging to allowed categories open normally within the user's browser.
The URL Filtering page shows a recommended setup to route internet traffic when users visit websites matching each of the specified URL categories.
You can drag the URL categories to the Block, Isolate, or Allow columns to set up the filtering policy appropriate for your organization.

ssl-defaults.statement: The SSL/TLS Inspection review step says Zscaler installs its recommended SSL/TLS Inspection policies by default. Separately, the step's Exempted Categories review says the Healthcare and Finance categories are not inspected because they might contain a user's personally identifiable information (PII); categories that are not exempted have their SSL/TLS traffic inspected under All Users, All Other Destinations; and Zscaler's intermediate root certificate is installed under SSL Root Certificate.

quotes: These categories (Healthcare and Finance) are not inspected because they might contain a user's personally identifiable information (PII).
Under Exempted Categories, review the categories that Zscaler exempts from SSL/TLS inspection.
Under All Users, All Other Destinations, note that categories that are not exempted have their SSL/TLS traffic inspected.
Under SSL Root Certificate, Zscaler's intermediate root certificate is installed.
Zscaler installs its recommended SSL/TLS Inspection policies by default.

ssl-m365.statement: By default Zscaler inspects SSL/TLS traffic from Microsoft's web-based applications such as OneDrive; Microsoft's recommended setting, which exempts that traffic, is selected as M365 Exempted under Advanced SSL Settings and saved.

quotes: By default, Zscaler inspects SSL/TLS traffic from Microsoft's web-based applications such as OneDrive.
If you want to use Microsoft's recommended setting, which exempts that traffic from SSL/TLS inspection, click Advanced SSL Settings, select M365 Exempted, and click Save.

cyber-defaults.statement: During onboarding Zscaler sets up its default cyber threat protection policies: Isolation (suspicious URLs not yet categorized, including newly registered URLs, dormant URLs and URLs not yet observed and categorized by Zscaler, open in a remote browser in a Zscaler data center), Botnet Protection, Phishing & Fraud Protection (also blocking adware, spyware, web spam and cryptomining), Malicious Active Content Prevention, P2P File Sharing Protection, Malware Protection (inbound and outbound traffic, HTTP, FTP and FTP over HTTP, using signature-based detection and malware feeds from trusted industry partners) and Zero-Day Attack Protection (zero-day threats isolated and analyzed in a sandbox environment).

quotes: During onboarding, Zscaler sets up its default cyber threat protection policies.

Isolation: Uses browser isolation to open suspicious URLs which have not yet been categorized in a remote browser in a Zscaler data center. These include newly registered URLs, dormant URLs, as well as URLs which have not yet been observed and categorized by Zscaler.

Botnet Protection: Protects your users from botnets with a series of methods including blocking known command and control (C2) servers, blocking domain generation algorithms, and examining potential botnet traffic.
Phishing & Fraud Protection: Blocks known and suspected phishing sites, and blocks adware, spyware, web spam, and cryptomining to protect your users from fraud.
Malicious Active Content Prevention: Blocks a number of vulnerabilities that might cause users to download malware
P2P File Sharing Protection: Blocks the use of peer-to-peer file-sharing applications, many of which encrypt content so they cannot be inspected for data leakage.

Malware Protection: Blocks malware by inspecting inbound and outbound traffic, HTTP, FTP, and FTP over HTTP using signature-based detection and protection using malware feeds from trusted industry partners.
Zero-Day Attack Protection: Isolates and analyzes zero-day threats in a sandbox environment.

data-protection-defaults.statement: During onboarding Zscaler sets up its default set of data protection policies; the review shows Visibility & Classification (Data Loss Prevention (DLP) dictionaries contain algorithms to inspect user traffic for potential data leakage, such as bank information, PII and sensitive file formats) and the Data Classification Dashboard (high-level visibility and insight into the organization's DLP content).

quotes: During onboarding, Zscaler sets up its default set of data protection policies.

Visibility & Classification: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) dictionaries contain algorithms to inspect user traffic for potential data leakage, such as bank information, PII, sensitive file formats and more.
Data Classification Dashboard: This dashboard gives you high-level visibility and insight into your organization's DLP content.

device-info-default.statement: On the onboarding privacy page, when the setting to collect device owner information and traffic is enabled, administrators can view user device information (device hostname, device owner and device name) in dashboards, reports or insights; the setting is enabled by default and should be disabled where required by law, such as regions governed by the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

quotes: You can configure User Privacy policies after you have set up Cyber Threat Protection policies

Collect device owner information and traffic: When this setting is enabled, administrators in your organization are able to view user device information (i.e., device hostname, device owner, and device name) when they view dashboards, reports, or insights.
This setting is enabled by default; it should be disabled where required by law, such as regions governed by the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

crash-reporting-setting.statement: On the onboarding privacy page, when Enable automatic crash reporting is enabled the Zscaler service uploads reports of system crashes experienced by users for analysis, which might contain user identifiable information; the page says this setting is disabled by default in compliance with GDPR.

quotes: Enable automatic crash reporting: When this setting is enabled, the Zscaler service uploads reports of system crashes experienced by your users for analysis.
These reports might contain user identifiable information.
This setting is disabled by default in compliance with GDPR.

blocked-countries.statement: The Miscellaneous page's Block Countries setting can block internet traffic to and from web servers based in specific countries.

quotes: You can block internet traffic to and from web servers based in specific countries.
To block countries, on the Miscellaneous page, under Block Countries:

onboarding-logo.statement: The company logo used in application banners, notifications and emails sent to users regarding security issues must be 300 x 220 pixels or less, 10 KB or less, and a PNG, JPG or GIF file; if the logo needs to be edited later, the page points to Administration > Account Management > Branding.

quotes: You can customize the Zscaler Admin Console to include your logo in application banners, notifications, and emails sent to your users regarding security issues.
Dimensions of 300 x 220 pixels or less
Size of 10 KB or less
PNG, JPG, or GIF file types
If you need to edit the logo later, you can go to Administration > Account Management > Branding.

review-and-activate.statement: The final onboarding step displays all the policy configurations the admin selected, each can be changed by clicking the Edit icon to return to that section, and Activate and Launch activates Zscaler with the selected policies and launches the Networking dashboard in the Zscaler Admin Console.

quotes: The final onboarding step displays all the policy configurations you have selected.
To make changes to any set of policies, click the Edit icon to return to that section.
Click Activate and Launch to activate Zscaler with the policies you have selected and launch the Networking dashboard in the Zscaler Admin Console.

activate-and-launch.statement: When the initial policy configuration is defined, Activate & Launch enables the selected policies and launches the Zscaler Admin Console, where the Networking dashboard is displayed by default.

quotes: When you have finished defining your initial policy configuration, click Activate & Launch to enable the policies you have selected and launch the Zscaler Admin Console.
the Networking dashboard in the Zscaler Admin Console is displayed by default

crash-reporting-default.summary: The onboarding privacy page says automatic crash reporting is disabled by default; the Client Connector page says the Android app automatically uploads crash reports and Zscaler recommends enabling the feature.

quotes: Enable automatic crash reporting: When this setting is enabled, the Zscaler service uploads reports of system crashes experienced by your users for analysis.
This setting is disabled by default in compliance with GDPR.

positions.says: The Enable automatic crash reporting setting is disabled by default in compliance with GDPR.

quotes: For the Android version of Zscaler Client Connector, the app automatically uploads crash reports, which might contain user-identifiable information.
Zscaler recommends that you enable this feature, because the crash reports provide crucial information for resolving unexpected issues.

positions.says: The Android Client Connector app automatically uploads crash reports, and Zscaler recommends enabling the feature (existing claim zcc.web-privacy.collection:crash-reports).

crash-reporting-default.impact: The default and the recommendation differ between the two pages; neither says the onboarding toggle and the Client Connector option are the same setting, so whether one governs the other is unsettled.

global-admins-group-name.title: Whether the Authentication Service Global Administrators group is the Zscaler Global Administrators group
global-admins-group-name.detail: The onboarding page names the Full Admin group Authentication Service Global Administrators; the Authentication Service groups page names the initial group with global administrative entitlements Zscaler Global Administrators (zidentity.groups:predefined-groups). Neither page says the two names are one group or that one was renamed.

idp-token-and-list.title: The SCIM bearer token's lifetime and the list of commonly used IdPs
idp-token-and-list.detail: The onboarding users page does not give the generated bearer token's lifetime or the list of commonly used IdPs.

csv-group-names.title: How many group values the Group Names column takes, and the onboarding CSV row limit
csv-group-names.detail: The Group Names column shows several group values only in an example row, and the onboarding page states no row limit (the Authentication Service import page gives 1,000: zidentity.users:csv-import-format).

default-categories.title: Which categories the recommended onboarding policies use
default-categories.detail: Which URL categories the recommended URL Filtering setup puts in Block, Isolate and Allow appears only in screenshots on the onboarding pages, as does the cyber and data protection defaults beyond their category names.

logo-identity.title: Whether the onboarding, Branding and organization-profile logos are one image
logo-identity.detail: The onboarding page gives 10 KB, the Branding page 70 KB and the organization profile 10 KB (see the logo-size divergence in unified.account-management); none says whether they are the same logo. The 300 x 220 pixel bound appears only on the onboarding page.
